newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Bank Zachodni, U.S. FFG fund to set up fund.
newsitem.headline: Polish Bank Zachodni, U.S. FFG fund to set up fund.

text.p: Polish state-owned commercial Bank Zachodni SA and the New York-based mutual fund company Forum Financial Group have set up a mutual-trust fund company, Zachodni's spokeswoman said on Thursday.

Lidia Wietrzynka said in a statement that Zachodni and Forum Financial Group had 50 percent stakes in the new firm, Zachodnie Towarzystwo Funduszy Powierniczych SA, which has a share capital of four million zlotys.

"We think there is still plenty of room for mutual trust funds on the Polish market...and that their number will quickly rise, becoming an important and stable element of the financial market," Wietrzynska said.
"Poles have placed only 1.5 percent of their savings wih mutual trust funds compared with 15-20 percent in western Europe and 25 percent in the U.S.," she said.
The new company has applied to the Polish Securities Commission (KPW) for an operating licence and is awaiting the KPW's decision, the statement said.
There are currently five mutual fund companies operating in Poland -- Pioneer, Korona, Przymierze, Fidelia and Atut, and two others have applied for a licence.
